title: Opt-in fail-closed blocks installs when the sigstore verifier is removed

prerequisites: An attacker who already has write access to node_modules (can delete the installed sigstore package) and wants to install a package whose provenance would fail to verify, in a project that has opted into strict provenance tooling
attacker.goal: Slip a package past provenance enforcement by making the verification tool absent, so the check degrades to a warning instead of blocking.

startingState: The project sets provenance.toolingUnavailable: "fail-closed". sigstore was installed; the attacker deletes it, then installs a non-sigstore package. Because the verifier is now missing, provenance cannot be evaluated for any package.
vulnerableVersion: n/a — defended by the provenance.toolingUnavailable: fail-closed knob (added after issue #56); the default warn mode is the documented limit in provenance-tooling-removed
expectedVerdict: attestation-tooling-unavailable: every non-sigstore install is blocked while the verifier is absent, on the reasoning that a missing verifier is itself suspicious. The sigstore bootstrap install (requested.name === "sigstore") stays exempt so it can never deadlock
regressionTest: tests/policy.test.ts > blocks when the sigstore tool is unavailable and toolingUnavailable is fail-closed
provenance: Closes the default-mode residual documented in provenance-tooling-removed. The knob is opt-in (default warn) because a fresh environment without sigstore must still be able to bootstrap it; a project that has already installed sigstore and wants to keep it that way sets fail-closed and gets a block instead of a warning if it is ever removed.
